shifts.summary: Overall the shift was reported as Moderate by most sources. Reasoning was generally easy, with many candidates attempting all questions. GA difficulty varied but leaned moderate, while Quant was easy to moderate and English easy. Good attempts ranged from the low 70s to the high 80s.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was described as simple and top‑notch. Options in non‑verbal questions looked similar and were time‑consuming. Statement‑based and blood‑relation items were present.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GS questions were tough for some, but many were as expected from previous years. Topics covered history, art, economics, current affairs and specific static GK items.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math was the toughest part for some, with many mensuration and trigonometry items. Arithmetic questions were few, and formula‑based problems were manageable with practice.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was comfortable with previous‑year passages and cloze tests. Some new phrasal verbs appeared and spelling questions were asked.

intro: The analysis for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 9 October 2026 is based on shift reports from candidates. Figures such as the number of good attempts are unofficial and reflect the observations of those who have shared their experiences. SSC normalises scores across shifts, so raw attempt counts may not directly translate to final marks. Shift 3 has not yet been analysed; its details will be added after the shift concludes.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty reported for the 9 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was reported as Moderate by most sources, while Shift 2 was reported as Easy. Shift 3 has not yet been analysed.

faqs.q: How many good attempts did candidates make on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: In Shift 1, good attempts ranged from 72 to 89 overall. In Shift 2, the average was about 85 attempts. No data is available for Shift 3 at this time.

faqs.q: Did time shortage affect any sections on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Candidates for Shift 2 noted that time shortage impacted the mathematics section and long reading passages.

faqs.q: Will the analysis for Shift 3 on 9 October 2026 be updated?
faqs.a: Yes, the analysis for Shift 3 will be added after the shift ends and sufficient candidate reviews are available.

faqs.q: How does SSC handle score differences across shifts for the 9 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure fairness, so variations in difficulty or attempt counts are adjusted in the final scoring.
